# Estimation Versus Hypothesis Testing {#sec-estimate-vs-test}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Distinguish precision planning from power planning.
- Recognise what a confidence interval and statistical test answer.
:::

## The idea

For **estimation**, the planning target is usually a specified interval width or precision. For **hypothesis testing**, the target typically specifies a null value, plausible alternative, significance threshold and probability of rejection under that alternative (power). The same outcome, such as a proportion, can lead to very different sample sizes for these two purposes.

## When and how to apply it

A confidence interval describes values compatible with observed data under the stated model. A power calculation is prospective and depends on a selected alternative; it does not estimate the probability that the research hypothesis is true. Planning must specify which question is primary.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Compare “estimate anaemia prevalence within five percentage points” with “test whether two regimens differ in anaemia risk by ten percentage points.”
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
A non-significant test is not evidence of equivalence.
:::
